article.Citation/Title: Luquiens, A., Belahda, D., Graux, C., Igounenc, N., Serrand, C., Rochefort, P., Mura, T., & Sergent, F. (2025). Psilocybin in alcohol use disorder and comorbid depressive symptoms: Results from a feasibility randomized clinical trial. Addiction.
article.SourcePDF: alcohol/Addiction - 2025 - Luquiens - Psilocybin in alcohol use disorder and comorbid depressive symptoms  Results from a.pdf
article.InterventionDescription: Two oral psilocybin sessions (25 mg experimental vs 1 mg control) 3 weeks apart, with preparation and integration psychotherapy, inpatient rehab setting, add-on to usual relapse-prevention care.

ae_events.Description: Myocardial infarction 3 days before scheduled 2nd dosing session, attributed to undiagnosed coronary artery disease; judged unrelated to psilocybin; prevented 2nd dose administration.
Two spontaneously resolving episodes of dizziness in one 25 mg-group participant during a dosing session; Table 4 lists dizziness in 2 (10%) patients.
Nightmares beginning 2 days after the first 25 mg dosing session, persisting 9 days; attributed to treatment.
Hypoglycemia at the end of a dosing session in a patient with comorbid anorexia; resolved with a snack; attributed to treatment.
Suicidal ideation: one 1 mg-group patient after suspecting group assignment; two 25 mg-group patients during heavy-drinking occasions after discharge.
Suicide attempt by a 1 mg-group patient 1 month after the first dosing session, coinciding with alcohol relapse and a stressful life event.
Headache in 2 (10%) 25 mg-group patients; not attributed to treatment.
Diarrhea in 1 (5%) 25 mg-group patient; not attributed to treatment.
Nausea in 1 (5%) 25 mg-group patient; not attributed to treatment.
Gastroenteritis in 1 (5%) 25 mg-group patient; not attributed to treatment.
Rumination in 1 (10%) 1 mg-group patient; not attributed to treatment.
Fatigue in 1 (5%) 25 mg-group patient; attributability to treatment not assessed (marked NA in Table 4).
Hospitalization for AUD relapse in 2 (10%) 25 mg-group patients; not attributed to treatment.
Ocular hypertension in 1 (5%) 25 mg-group patient; not attributed to treatment.
Ankle sprain in 1 (10%) 1 mg-group patient; not attributed to treatment.
Breast lump discovered on entry examination before treatment began, in 1 (5%) 25 mg-group patient; not attributed to treatment.
Cough in 1 (5%) 25 mg-group patient; not attributed to treatment.
Palpebral (eyelid) abscess in 1 (10%) 1 mg-group patient; not attributed to treatment.
COVID-19/non-specific viral illness in 1 (10%) 1 mg-group patient and 1 (5%) 25 mg-group patient; not attributed to treatment.

article.Outcome: Primary outcome is explicitly feasibility ('The primary outcome was feasibility, assessed as the number of patients completing both psilocybin sessions, and screening and inclusion rates' — Abstract Measurements, Methods 'Measures'). The Statistical analysis section names the primary-endpoint test explicitly ('The rate of patients completing both dosing sessions (primary endpoint) was compared between groups via a Fischer test'). Results 'Feasibility' section reports this comparison: 95% (19/20) in the 25 mg group vs 60% (6/10) in the 1 mg group, P=0.031. This is a feasibility endpoint, not a substance-use outcome; the key SUD-related secondary outcome was 12-week abstinence (55% vs 11%, P=0.043; Table 2, Results 'Preliminary efficacy'), reported here for transparency but not used as Outcome per the boundary-case rule that Outcome must be the stated primary even when the SUD outcome is only secondary.
article.SD: Fisher's exact test was used for the primary feasibility comparison (2nd-dose completion); the article reports only the resulting P-value (0.031, Results 'Feasibility'), with no separate test statistic (e.g., chi-square value) printed for this comparison. Coded '.'.
article.PVal: P=0.031 for 2nd-dose completion (95% vs 60%), reported verbatim in Results 'Feasibility' section ('P-value = 0.031').
article.SampleSize_NFinal: The feasibility/primary-endpoint comparison (2nd-dose completion) was computed over the full randomized, as-treated per-protocol sample: n=20 (25 mg) + n=10 (1 mg) = 30, consistent with the reported percentages (19/20=95%, 6/10=60%).

MethodologyDescribedYN.note: All 14 elements are explicitly described: objective (Abstract/Introduction aims), design (Methods 'Design' — prospective, single-center, double-blind, 2:1 parallel RCT pilot), setting (French inpatient addiction unit, CHU Nîmes), eligibility (detailed inclusion/exclusion lists), intervention (dosing/preparation/integration protocol described in detail), comparator (1 mg psilocybin arm described), outcomes (Measures section defines primary and secondary outcomes), sample_size_power (dedicated 'Sample size' subsection citing Hertzog's pilot-study sizing method; no formal power calculation but the determination is explicitly described and justified), randomization (SAS-generated sequence, stratified by gender, permuted block sizes 3/6, implemented via Inclusio software), blinding (double-blind design described, plus a formal blinding-integrity assessment), statistical_methods (detailed 'Statistical analysis' section), results (comprehensive Results with tables/figures), harms (dedicated 'Safety' section and AE Table 4), funding_coi (Funding information section names the grant; 'Declaration of interests: None').

article.Pos Result Y/N: Coded 1: the stated primary (feasibility) endpoint succeeded (95% vs 60% 2nd-dose completion, P=0.031) and the study concluded psilocybin therapy was feasible, acceptable and safe; the SUD-related secondary outcomes also favored the 25 mg group (12-week abstinence 55% vs 11%, P=0.043; % change in drinking days P=0.038; craving frequency P=0.045), giving a consistent positive direction across primary and key secondary endpoints.
article.PrimaryCare: Study conducted in a specialized inpatient addiction/rehabilitation unit (CHU Nîmes), not a primary-care setting; no primary-care setting or provider involvement is described anywhere in the article. Coded 0.
article.Power: No formal a priori power calculation is reported; the 20:10 sample size was determined per Hertzog's pilot-study sample-size recommendations (Statistical analysis, 'Sample size'), not a power analysis. However, the Discussion explicitly states a possible 'lack of power' for the antidepressant-subgroup comparison, which per the rubric's rule ('a bare statement that the study was underpowered counts as discussed') is coded 1.
article.Retention (%): 30 participants randomized and analyzed as-treated (20:10, per-protocol). The Statistical analysis section states 'only 1 week 12 endpoint was missing' (one 1 mg-group participant lost to follow-up before week 12); no other losses to the analyzed population are reported. 29/30 = 96.7%. Denominator is the randomized N (30) per rule, since randomized and as-treated N coincide here.
article.ConfoundYN: Coded 1: the study explicitly assessed subgroup/moderator effects — antidepressant use on drinking/depression outcomes (Table 3, dedicated subsection), and baseline PCL-5 as a factor associated with abstinence response.
article.Age_Median: Abstract reports mean age 49 ± 10; Table 1 reports median age 50 (IQR 42-57). The two values straddle the '30-50'/'50+' bracket boundary. Coded '30-50' based on the explicitly-labeled mean (49), noting the median (50) sits exactly at the bracket boundary.
article.RaceEthnicity_BIPOCPercent: Race/ethnicity data are not reported anywhere in the article (French single-center cohort). Coded '.'.
article.Country_USvsNonUS: Single-center study at CHU Nîmes, France; approved by the French Ethics Committee (Comité de Protection des Personnes) and French national medicines agency. Coded 'NonUS'.
article.RecruitmentRepresentYN: Coded 0: highly selected volunteer sample — 350 screened, 30 enrolled (8.6%) after extensive psychiatric/medical exclusion criteria (psychosis/bipolar history, severe personality disorder, prior hallucinogen use, numerous medical contraindications, etc.); recruitment was substantially driven by media exposure and self-referral ('The study received high media exposure, leading to proactive outreach'; 98% of requests were spontaneous), not reflective of the general severe-AUD treatment-seeking population.
article.Comparator: Comparator is a very-low-dose (1 mg) psilocybin arm used as an active/blinding comparator rather than an inert placebo or no-treatment control (a dose-comparison design); coded 1 per the rule that dose-comparison designs count as a comparator.
article.InterventionTherapy: Coded 1: structured preparation (day before) and integration (day after) psychotherapy sessions accompany both dosing sessions, plus non-directive supportive psychotherapy during dosing itself, per a study therapeutic manual.
article.Followup in months: Longest follow-up assessment was at week 12 post-inclusion (12 weeks / 4 = 3 months). This horizon is measured from inclusion/baseline (not end of treatment) and is used consistently for the week-3/6/12 assessment schedule throughout the article (2nd dose occurs at week 3), so there is no separate end-of-treatment horizon to reconcile against.
article.MortalityMeasured: No deaths occurred or were reported anywhere in the article; the complete AE listing (Table 4) contains no fatal event. Mortality was not established as a formal outcome measure. Coded 0 (rather than '.') since the absence of any death is confirmable from the exhaustive AE table and narrative.
article.ArmScope: Both study arms (25 mg and 1 mg) received psilocybin — there is no non-exposed comparator; the 'control' arm is a low, sub-active dose, not a placebo. Coded 'psychedelic_arm' because the entire per-protocol sample (n=30) is psilocybin-exposed by design, even though Table 4 breaks AE counts out by dose group; NumDistinctAEs (19), NParticipantsWithAE (16, = 10 in 25 mg + 6 in 1 mg) and AE_denominator (30) aggregate across both dose groups accordingly.

ae_events.Luquiens 2025_AE01: Onset coded 'delayed' (event occurred about 3 weeks after the first dose, days before the scheduled second); severity Severe as a life-threatening cardiovascular event (FDA seriousness criterion), though the article states it was unrelated to treatment. InterventionRequired coded '.' since the article does not describe the clinical management given.
ae_events.Luquiens 2025_AE02: NAffected coded 2 to match Table 4's '2 (10%)' attributable count; the Safety narrative describes 'two episodes... in the same participant', which may mean only 1 patient experienced both episodes rather than 2 separate patients each having one — flagged as a minor internal inconsistency between narrative and table.
ae_events.Luquiens 2025_AE03: Graded Moderate per rubric because the nightmares persisted 9 days (sleep disturbance lasting days-to-weeks, no FDA seriousness criterion met), rather than Mild; no explicit intervention is mentioned.
ae_events.Luquiens 2025_AE04: Graded Moderate because resolution required an active (if minimal/noninvasive) intervention — a snack — analogous to a CTCAE Grade 2 event, rather than a no-intervention Mild event.
ae_events.Luquiens 2025_AE05: SeverityIndeterminate=Y: the article does not describe plan, intent, or clinical intervention for any of the three ideation events, only that they occurred; per rubric, underspecified AEs default to Mild with this flag set, given the safety-sensitive nature of suicidal ideation this is flagged for human review. NAffected=3 sums the 1 mg-group case (1, attributable) and the 25 mg-group cases (2, not attributable), all described in the Safety 'Suicidal risk' narrative.
ae_events.Luquiens 2025_AE06: Graded Severe per the rubric's explicit PAT-specific list ('suicidal behavior/attempt' is automatically Severe); the article states this event was not attributable to treatment.

config_proposal.note: Primary endpoint is feasibility (2nd-dose completion: 95% [19/20] vs 60% [6/10], Fisher's exact P=0.031), not a substance-use outcome; computed as an odds ratio from the two-group proportions per codebook precedence. Coded approx (not clean) both because a proportion-to-OR conversion is an assumption a methodologist should see, and because this is a feasibility rather than SUD-behavioral effect size — a human reviewer may prefer substituting the 12-week abstinence secondary outcome (55% vs 11%, P=0.043, OR computable similarly) for the SUD-specific forest plot.
